title: Landing film scope
question: The handoff includes a full scroll-chapter landing. How much of that film experience should replace the current page in the first ship?

options.label: Full five chapters
options.thesis: Port Sitewise Landing.dc.html as designed: five scroll chapters over the full 106s film, then CTA and footer.
options.viewport: Sticky film stage left-copy overlays; one chapter per scroll snap; Get started close.
options.risk: Largest port: two WebGL cube stages, canvas screen content, chapter clock, reduced-motion plan.
options.case: Matches the authored landing shell exactly; nothing from the old facet story survives.

options.label: Landing cut only
options.thesis: Ship Reveal + Invoice from Sitewise Landing Film first; add Profile and Transmittal in a follow-up.
options.viewport: Same dark nav and sticky stage, but only two scroll chapters before the CTA.
options.risk: Faster to land, but the page feels unfinished if visitors expect the full product story.
options.case: Useful if you want a working page sooner and will finish the later acts next.

options.label: Shell first, film later
options.thesis: Replace nav, copy, CTA, and tokens now; keep a still or short loop of the mark until the chapter engine is ready.
options.viewport: Handoff layout and type with a non-interactive cube or poster frame.
options.risk: Loses the memorable moment that makes this handoff worth shipping.
options.case: Only if motion is blocked; otherwise underdelivers the brief.
